newsitem.title: USA: USWC gasolines steady to lower, "clear" tightens.
newsitem.headline: USWC gasolines steady to lower, "clear" tightens.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast gasoline were steady to lower late Monday, while rumors arose that the price of conventional, or "clear" gasoline was closing in on CARB-grades, traders said.
Meanwhile, crude oil for May delivery made strong gains as NYMEX traders bought the contract to cover their shorts, a position which meant they initially though prices would fall.
Nearby crude rose 47 cents a barrel to $20.38 in late trade, while unleaded gasoline climbed 1.31 cents a gallon.
Traders scrambled before the May crude contract expired Tuesday.

April/May prices for CARB (California Air Resources Board) unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles were talked one cent higher than Friday at 72 to 73 cents, with some traders noting a year-on-year drop in West Coast stocks lent support.
San Francisco CARB cost the same Monday.
Earlier, a swap of CARB for conventional gasoline was reported by a large refiner Monday. The deal involved an unknown quantity of CARB for conventional, which stood 5.5 cents a gallon cheaper.
But afternoon trade saw CARB trade five cents over conventional.
Two cargoes of CARB were slated to arrive this week, but traders did not immediately know when they would come.
L.A. low sulphur diesel dropped 1.50 cents a gallon to 59.50/61 cents, with traders saying a cargo of fuel was delivered
